title: `extensions` negotiation
description: The opt-in mechanism for everything outside the core protocol, keyed by a vendor-prefixed extension name and declared by both sides.
question: Can the framework negotiate an extension at all?
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
why: Extensions are disabled by default and require explicit support from both sides. This row is the gate in front of every other extension: without it, Tasks and Apps are unreachable regardless of what the framework implements internally.

notes.openai-agents: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.23.1: the client sends no `extensions` in its capabilities, and nothing in `agents.mcp` accepts one to pass through, so the fixture's offer of `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` goes unanswered.
notes.pydantic-ai: Pydantic AI 2.54.0: the default `MCPToolset` sends no `extensions` in its capabilities. FastMCP 4 folds in client extensions that are registered, and Pydantic AI registers only the optional `fastmcp_tasks` package, which the pinned install does not include.
notes.mastra: Mastra 2.2.0: every `MCPClient` session declares `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` under `extensions`, merged with any configured through `capabilities.extensions`. Measured as the declaration on the wire; what Mastra does with the server's reply is not.
notes.vercel_ai: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): the default client sends no `extensions` in its capabilities, so nothing was negotiated with a server offering `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui`. Extensions can be declared through the `capabilities` option (the package exports `mcpAppClientCapabilities` for MCP Apps); that path was not measured.
notes.strands: Strands Agents 1.59.0: The client declares no extensions, so the `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` extension the fixture offers is never negotiated.
notes.agno: Agno 3.1.2: the fastmcp `Client` `MCPTools` builds declares no extensions, so the `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` extension the fixture offers is never negotiated.
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: neither DSPy nor the caller's `mcp.Client` declares extensions, so the fixture's offered `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` is never negotiated.
notes.langchain_js: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): the client opens with its first request (no `server/discover`) and sends empty capabilities with no `extensions`, so the fixture's offer of `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` goes unanswered.
notes.copilot_sdk: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): the client declares no `extensions`, so the fixture's `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` was not negotiated.
notes.langchain4j: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: `DefaultMcpClient` declares no extensions and ignores the ones the server offers.
notes.google_adk_go: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): the client declares no `extensions`, so the fixture's `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` was not negotiated.
notes.ms_agent_framework_dotnet: Microsoft Agent Framework (.NET) 1.24.0 (ModelContextProtocol 2.2.0): the client declares no `extensions`, so the fixture's `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` was not negotiated.
notes.openai_agents_js: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: the client opens with its first request (no `server/discover`) and sends empty capabilities with no `extensions`, so the fixture's offer of `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` goes unanswered.
